text: Retrieval augmented generation answers a question by first retrieving relevant passages from a document collection and then generating an answer grounded in those passages. The retriever usually embeds documents and the query into vectors and returns the nearest neighbours by cosine similarity. Good chunking matters: chunks that are too large dilute the signal, chunks that are too small lose context, and a small overlap between chunks preserves sentences split at a boundary.
title: RAG basics

text: A RAG system is evaluated on a golden set of questions with known answers. Recall at k measures whether the correct document appears in the top k retrieved passages, and mean reciprocal rank rewards putting the correct document first. A retrieval eval must be run before any generator is judged, because a generator cannot answer well from passages that were never retrieved. Hallucination checks compare the final answer against the retrieved passages, not against the model's general knowledge.
title: Evaluating a RAG system

text: Chunking splits long documents into retrievable pieces. Fixed size chunking cuts text every few hundred words, sentence chunking keeps whole sentences together, and recursive chunking tries paragraph then sentence then word boundaries. Overlap between neighbouring chunks helps when a key sentence sits on a boundary. The right chunk size is measured on the eval set, not guessed: try several sizes and keep the one with the best recall at k.
title: Chunking strategies

text: Embeddings turn text into dense vectors so that similar meanings land close together in vector space. A vector database stores those embeddings and returns approximate nearest neighbours quickly even for millions of documents. Sparse retrieval such as TF-IDF instead matches exact words weighted by rarity, which is strong when questions reuse the documents' own vocabulary. Hybrid search combines dense and sparse scores to cover both paraphrase and exact term matches.
title: Embeddings and vector search

text: Prompt caching reuses the computation for a repeated prompt prefix instead of processing it again. When many requests share a long system prompt or the same retrieved context, the cache hit rate rises and cost per request falls. Cache effectiveness is measured as the share of input tokens served from cache and the resulting cost before and after caching, on the same workload, not on cherry picked prompts.
title: Prompt caching

text: Agent guardrails limit what an autonomous agent may do without approval. A common pattern is an approval gate before any irreversible action such as sending a message, spending money, or deleting files, while read only actions proceed freely. Guardrails also include input filters that block prompt injection attempts, output checks that verify claims against retrieved sources, and retry caps that stop an agent looping forever on a failing step.
title: Agent guardrails

text: Testing Python code with the standard library unittest module needs no extra installation. A good test checks one behaviour, uses a small known input, and asserts an exact expected output rather than a vague property. Unit tests cover individual functions, integration tests cover the whole pipeline end to end, and a test that was never run is not evidence: the suite must be executed and its pass count reported honestly.
title: Testing Python code

text: A Git workflow starts by creating a branch for one change, committing small focused changes with clear messages, and opening a pull request for review. The main branch stays deployable, so unfinished work lives on a feature branch until it is reviewed and tested. Before pushing, run the tests locally and read back the remote state after pushing, because a push that was interrupted may already have landed.
title: Git workflow basics
